x: Commentary on Surah "A-ra'ayta" (Have You Seen) [Surah al-Ma'un]
The discussion on the interpretation of the words of the Mighty, whose praise is majestic:
h

Have you seen the one who denies the Recompense (1) That is the one who repels the orphan (2) and does not urge the feeding of the poor (3) So woe to those who pray (4) who are heedless of their prayer (5) those who show off (6) and withhold al-ma'un (7)
The Exalted means by His words:
h
Have you seen the one who denies the Recompense (1)
: Have you seen, Muhammad, the one who denies God's reward and punishment, and so does not obey Him in His commands and prohibitions?
The people of interpretation said something similar to what we have said about that.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father told me, saying: My uncle told me, saying: My father told me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas
m: Have you seen the one who denies the Recompense
. He said: The one who denies the judgment of God, Mighty and Majestic

c: Al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan told us, saying: Warqa' told us, from [Ibn Jurayj:
m: . It is mentioned that in the reading of 'Abd Allah it is: (a-ra'aytaka
in his reading is a redundant particle; its presence in the speech and its absence are the same.

evidence.text: It is mentioned that in the reading of 'Abd Allah it is: (a-ra'aytaka (1) alladhi yukadhdhibu (2)).
The kaf (3) in his reading is a redundant particle; its presence in the speech and its absence are the same.

x: And His words:
h
That is the one who repels the orphan

. He says: This one who denies the Recompense is the one who pushes the orphan away from his right and wrongs him. One says of it: "da'a'tu fulanan 'an haqqihi" - I pushed so-and-so away from his right - "fa-ana ada'u'hu da'an".
The people of interpretation said something similar to what we have said about that.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father told me, saying: My uncle told me, saying: My father told me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas:
m: That is the one who repels the orphan
. He said: He withholds the orphan's right.

c: Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim told us, saying: 'Isa told us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan told us, saying: Warqa' told us,
m: both from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid regarding the words of God:
. He said: He pushes the orphan away and does not feed him

c: Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid told us, saying: Sa'id told us, from Qatada:
m: That is the one who repels the orphan
. That is: He overpowers him and wrongs him.

c: Ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr told us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada:
m: . He said: He overpowers him and wrongs him

c: I was told from al-Husayn,
m: who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd told us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His words:

c: Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran told us, from Sufyan
m: . He said: He pushes him away.

x: And His words:
h
and does not urge the feeding of the poor
. The Exalted says: And he does not urge others to feed the one in need of food.
And His words:
h
So woe to those who pray (4) who are heedless of their prayer

. The Exalted says: So the valley that flows with the pus of the people of Hell is for the hypocrites who pray without intending God, Mighty and Majestic, by their prayer, and who are heedless in their prayer when they pray it.
The people of interpretation differed about the meaning of His words:
h
heedless of their prayer
Some of them said: What is meant by that is that they delay it beyond its time, and do not pray it until after its time has ended.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Sakan ibn Nafi' al-Bahili told us, saying: Shu'ba told us, from Khalaf ibn Hawshab, from Talha ibn Musarrif, from Mus'ab ibn Sa'd, who said:
m: I said to my father: What of the words of God, Mighty and Majestic:
who are heedless of their prayer
. Is it abandoning it? He said: No, but delaying it beyond its time

c: Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayya told us, from Hisham al-Dastuwa'i, who said: 'Asim ibn Bahdala told us, from Mus'ab ibn Sa'd, who said:
m: who are heedless of their prayer
. Is it what one of us tells himself in his prayer? He said: No, but heedlessness is that he delays it beyond its time

c: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki' told us, from Sufyan, from 'Asim, from Mus'ab ibn Sa'd:
m: who are heedless of their prayer
. He said: Heedlessness is leaving it past its time.

c: 'Amr ibn 'Ali narrated to us, saying: 'Imran ibn Tamam al-Bunani told us, saying:
m: al-Duba'i Nasr ibn 'Imran told us, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His words:
who are heedless of their prayer
. He said: Those who delay it beyond its time

c: Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Ya'qub told us, from Ja'far, from Ibn Abza:
m: So woe to those who pray (4) who are heedless of their prayer
. He said: Those who delay the obligatory prayer until it passes out of its time or beyond its time.

c: Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman told us, saying: Sufyan told us, from al-A'mash, from Abu al-Duha, from Masruq:
m: who are heedless of their prayer
. He said: Leaving it past its time.

c: Abu al-Sa'ib narrated to me, saying: Abu Mu'awiya told me, from al-A'mash, from Muslim, from Masruq
m: who are heedless of their prayer
. He said: Wasting its appointed time

c: Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran told us, from Sufyan, from al-A'mash, from Abu al-Duha:
m: . He said: Leaving the obligatory prayer past its time

c: Ibn al-Barqi narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi Maryam told us, saying: Yahya ibn Ayyub told us, saying: Ibn Zahr informed me, from al-A'mash, from Muslim ibn Subayh:
m: : Those who waste it beyond its time.

x: Others said: Rather, what is meant is that they abandon it and do not pray it at all.
Mention of those who said that:

c: 'Ali narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih told us, saying: Mu'awiya told me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas
m: So woe to those who pray (4) who are heedless of their prayer

: They are the hypocrites, who showed off to the people with their prayer when they were present, and abandoned it when they were absent, and withheld from them the loan of things out of hatred for them, and that is al-ma'un

c: Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father told me, saying: My uncle told me, saying: My father told me, from his father: from Ibn 'Abbas:
m: who are heedless of their prayer
. He said: They are the hypocrites who abandon prayer in private and pray in public

c: Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran told us, from Sufyan, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid:

x: Others said: Rather, what is meant is that they are lax about it, neglect it, and are distracted from it.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim told us, saying: 'Isa told us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan told us, saying: Warqa' told us,
m: both from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid regarding His words:

c: Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid told us, saying: Sa'id told us, from Qatada:
m: who are heedless of their prayer

c: Ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr told us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada:
m: . He said: Heedless of it, not caring whether he prays or does not pray

c: Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said
m: Those who are heedless of their prayer
: They pray, but prayer is not their concern

c: Abu al-Sa'ib narrated to me, saying: Ibn Fudayl told us, from Layth, from Mujahid
m: Those who are heedless of their prayer
. The most correct of the sayings on this, in my view, regarding His words

, is: distracted, neglecting it; and in being distracted from it and occupied with other things there is wasting it at times, and wasting its time at others. Since that is so, the saying of those who said that what is meant is abandoning its time is correct, and likewise the saying of those who said that what is meant is abandoning it, because of what I mentioned earlier, that heedlessness of it includes the meanings I mentioned. Two reports have been related from the Messenger of God, peace be upon him, which support the soundness of what we have said about that:

c: One of them is what Zakariya ibn Aban al-Misri narrated to me, saying: 'Amr ibn Tariq told us, saying: 'Ikrima ibn Ibrahim told us, saying: 'Abd al-Malik ibn 'Umayr told us, from Mus'ab ibn Sa'd, from Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, who said:
m: I asked the Prophet, peace be upon him, about:
Those who are heedless of their prayer
. He said: "They are those who delay the prayer beyond its time"

c: The other of them is what Abu Kurayb narrated to me, saying: Mu'awiya ibn Hisham told us, from Shayban al-Nahwi, from Jabir al-Ju'fi, who said: A man told me, from Abu Barza al-Aslami, who said:
m: The Messenger of God, peace be upon him, said when this verse was revealed:
Those who are heedless of their prayer

: "God is greatest! This is better for you than if every one of you were given the like of the whole world. It is he who, if he prays, does not hope for the good of his prayer, and if he abandons it, does not fear his Lord"

c: Abu 'Abd al-Rahim al-Barqi narrated to me, saying: 'Amr ibn Abi Salama told me, saying:
m: I heard 'Umar ibn Sulayman relate from 'Ata' ibn Dinar
that he said: Praise be to God who said:
Those who are heedless of their prayer
. Both meanings that I mentioned in the two reports we related from the Messenger of God, peace be upon him, are possible
within the meaning of heedlessness of prayer.

x: And His words:
h
those who show off

. He says: Those who show off to the people with their prayer when they pray; for they do not pray out of desire for reward nor fear of punishment, but only pray it so that the believers see them and think them to be of their number, and so refrain from shedding their blood and taking their children captive. They are the hypocrites who lived in the time of the Messenger of God, peace be upon him, who concealed disbelief and displayed Islam. Thus said the people of interpretation.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abu 'Amir and Mu'ammal told us,
m: both saying: Sufyan told us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid:
Those who are heedless of their prayer
. He said: They are the hypocrites

c: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki' told us, from Sufyan, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid,
Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran told us, from Sufyan, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid,
Yunus narrated to me, saying: Sufyan told us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, from 'Ali ibn Abi Talib,
m: may God be pleased with him, regarding His words:
those who show off (6) and withhold al-ma'un
. He said: They show off with their prayer

c: I was told from al-Husayn,
m: who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd told us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His words:
Those who are heedless of their prayer (5) those who show off

c: 'Ali narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih told us, saying: Mu'awiya told me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said:
m: They are the hypocrites; they used to show off to the people with their prayer when they were present, and abandon it when they were absent.

c: Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd told me:
m: And they pray - and prayer is not their concern - out of show.

x: And His words:
h
and withhold al-ma'un
. He says: And they withhold from the people the benefits of what they have. The root of al-ma'un is the benefit of anything; the water that comes down from the clouds is called its ma'un
n
. From it is the saying of A'sha of Banu Tha'laba
n
: None is more generous than he with his ma'un, when their sky does not become overcast. And another describing a cloud
n
: * Its heavy cloud pours out the ma'un in torrents * And 'Ubayd al-Ra'i said
n
: A people upon Islam, who have not yet withheld their ma'un nor wasted the tahlil. By ma'un he means obedience and zakat.
The people of interpretation differed about which of the meanings of ma'un is intended in this place.
Some of them said: What is meant by it is the obligatory zakat.

m: the same. He said: Waki' told us, from al-A'mash, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, the same; he said: The axe and the bucket

Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki' told us; and Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran told us, from Sufyan, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said:
Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki' told us, from Sufyan, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid,
Ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr told us,
m: , from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas, the same

c: Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to us, saying: Abu 'Asim told us, saying: 'Isa told us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan told us, saying: Warqa' told us,
m: both from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His words:

c: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Isma'il told us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid - I think from Ibn 'Abbas,
Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayya told us, saying: Ibn Abi Najih informed us, from Mujahid, who said: Ibn 'Abbas said:
'Ali narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih told us, saying: Mu'awiya told me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said:
m: They withhold from them the loan, and that is al-ma'un.

c: Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father told me, saying: My uncle told me, saying: My father told me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas:
m: . He said: People differed about that; some of them said: They withhold zakat. And some of them said: They withhold obedience. And some of them said: They withhold the loan

c: Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayya told us, from Layth, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas
m: . He said: Its people have not yet come

c: Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Muhammad told us, saying: Shu'ba told us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, who said: Ibn 'Abbas said:
Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, saying: Ibn 'Ulayya informed us, saying: Layth told us, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Harith, who said:
m: 'Ali, may God be pleased with him, said:
: Withholding zakat, the axe, the bucket and the cooking pot

c: Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abu 'Asim al-Nabil told us, saying: Sufyan told us, from Habib ibn Abi Thabit, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said:
Abu Husayn 'Abd Allah ibn Ahmad ibn Yunus narrated to me, saying: 'Abthar told us, saying: Husayn told us, from Abu Malik
m: . He said: The bucket, the cooking pot and the axe (2).

c: 'Amr ibn 'Ali narrated to us, saying: Abu Dawud told us, saying: Abu 'Awana told us, from 'Asim ibn Bahdala, from Abu Wa'il, from 'Abd Allah, who said:
m: We were with our Prophet, peace be upon him, and we used to say:
: Withholding the bucket and the like

x: Others said:
h
al-ma'un
: Kindness.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Sulami narrated to us, saying: Abu 'Asim told us, saying: Muhammad ibn Rifa'a told us, saying:
m: I heard Muhammad ibn Ka'b say:

x: Others said:
h
al-ma'un
: It is wealth.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Ahmad ibn Harb narrated to me, saying: Musa ibn Isma'il told us, saying: Ibrahim ibn Sa'd told us, from Ibn Shihab, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, who said:
m: Al-ma'un in the tongue of Quraysh is wealth

c: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki' told us, from Ibn Abi Dhi'b, from al-Zuhri, who said:
m: Al-ma'un in the tongue of Quraysh is wealth

. The most correct of the sayings on this, in our view - since al-ma'un is what we described earlier, and God has informed of these people that they withhold it from the people, a general report without singling out any part of it - is that it be said: God described them as withholding from the people what they lend one another in turns, and withholding from the needy and the poor the rights God made obligatory for them in their wealth; for all of that is among the benefits by which people benefit from one another. End of the commentary on Surah (A-ra'ayta).

notes.en: S and T1 read “they help one another.”
notes.ar: في ص، ت (1): (يتعاون).

notes.en: Reported by Ibn Abī Shayba, 2/202, through Abū Muʿāwiya.
notes.ar: أخرجه ابن أبي شيبة (2/ 202) عن أبى معاوية به.

notes.en: Reported by Ibn Abī Shayba, 2/203, through another route from Ibrāhīm.
notes.ar: أخرجه ابن أبي شيبة (2/ 203) من طريق آخر عن إبراهيم به.

notes.en: Reported by Ibn Abī Shayba, 2/203, and al-Bayhaqī, 4/183 and 6/88, through Wakīʿ. Al-Suyūṭī attributes it in al-Durr al-manthūr, 6/401, to Ādam, Saʿīd ibn Manṣūr, Ibn al-Mundhir, and al-Ḍiyāʾ in al-Mukhtāra.
notes.ar: أخرجه ابن أبي شيبة (2/ 203)، والبيهقى (4/ 183، 6/ 88) من طريق وكيع به، وعزاه السيوطى في الدر المنثور (6/ 401) إلى آدم وسعيد بن منصور وابن المنذر والضياء في المختارة.

notes.en: Al-Ṭabarānī in al-Kabīr (12354) and al-Ḥākim, 2/536, reported it through Sufyān.
notes.ar: أخرجه الطبراني في الكبير (12354)، والحاكم (2/ 536) من طريق سفيان به.

notes.en: Reported by ʿAbd al-Razzāq in his Tafsīr, 2/399, through Sufyān al-Thawrī.
notes.ar: أخرجه عبد الرزاق في تفسيره (2/ 399) عن سفيان الثورى به.

notes.en: T1 adds “from Qatāda” after this.
notes.ar: بعده في ت (1): (عن قتادة).

notes.en: Reported by ʿAbd al-Razzāq, 2/399, from Maʿmar.
notes.ar: أخرجه عبد الرزاق (2/ 399) عن معمر به.

notes.en: Tafsīr Mujāhid, p. 755; al-Bayhaqī, 4/183–184, reported it through him.
notes.ar: تفسير مجاهد ص (755)، ومن طريقه البيهقى (4/ 183، 184).

notes.en: Cited by Ibn Kathīr in his Tafsīr, 8/518; al-Suyūṭī attributes it to Ibn Mardawayh in al-Durr al-manthūr, 6/401.
notes.ar: ذكره ابن كثير في تفسيره (8/ 518)، وعزاه السيوطى في الدر المنثور (6/ 401) إلى ابن مردويه.

notes.en: Reported by Ibn Abī Shayba, 3/203, through Ibn ʿUlayya.
notes.ar: أخرجه ابن أبي شيبة (3/ 203) عن ابن علية به.

notes.en: Cited by Ibn Kathīr in his Tafsīr, 8/518, from al-Muṣannaf. Ibn Abī Shayba, 3/203, reported it through Ibn ʿUlayya.
notes.ar: ذكره ابن كثير في تفسيره (8/ 518) عن المصنف، وأخرجه ابن أبي شيبة (3/ 203) عن ابن علية به.

notes.en: Compare Ibn Kathīr’s Tafsīr, 8/517.
notes.ar: ينظر تفسير ابن كثير (8/ 517).

notes.en: Reported by Abū Dāwūd (1657), and through him by al-Bayhaqī, 4/183; al-Bazzār (1719); and al-Nasāʾī in al-Sunan al-kubrā (11701), through Abū ʿAwāna. It is also in Tafsīr Mujāhid, p. 755, and al-Bayhaqī, 4/183, through ʿĀṣim. Al-Ṭabarānī reported it in al-Awsaṭ (4589), through Abū Wāʾil.
notes.ar: أخرجه أبو داود (1657) - ومن طريقه البيهقى (4/ 183) - والبزار (1719)، والنسائى في الكبرى (11701) من طريق أبى عوانة به، وهو في تفسير مجاهد ص (755)، والبيهقى (4/ 183) من طريق عاصم، وأخرجه الطبراني في الأوسط (4589) من طريق أبى وائل به.

notes.en: Cited by Ibn Kathīr in his Tafsīr, 8/518.
notes.ar: ذكره ابن كثير في تفسيره (8/ 518).

notes.en: See ʿIlal Aḥmad, 2/58–59 (379).
notes.ar: ينظر علل أحمد (2/ 59،58) (379).

notes.en: Reported by Ibn Abī Shayba, 3/204 and 10/469–470, and by Ibn Abī Ḥātim, as cited in Ibn Kathīr’s Tafsīr, 8/518, through Wakīʿ.
notes.ar: أخرجه ابن أبي شيبة (3/ 204، 10/ 469، 470)، وابن أبي حاتم - كما في تفسير ابن كثير (8/ 518) - من طريق وكيع به.
